primary.title: The Gathas
primary.author: Zoroaster
primary.rationale: The Gathas are hymns attributed to Zoroaster himself and are considered the core of Zoroastrian scripture. They are central to understanding his teachings.

secondary.title: Zoroastrianism: An Introduction
secondary.author: Prods Oktor Skjærvø
secondary.rationale: A comprehensive and scholarly introduction to Zoroastrianism by a leading expert, covering its history, beliefs, and texts, including Zoroaster's life and teachings.

secondary.title: The Zoroastrian Flame: Its Origins, Philosophy, and Practice
secondary.author: R. C. Zaehner
secondary.rationale: While published in 1976, this is a foundational scholarly work on Zoroastrianism that remains highly influential for understanding the religion and its founder.

secondary.title: Zoroaster's Time and Homeland: A Survey of the Evidence
secondary.author: Mary Boyce
secondary.rationale: Although pre-1976, Mary Boyce's work is seminal in the academic study of Zoroastrianism, particularly regarding the historical context of Zoroaster. It is often cited in later scholarship.

suggestions.notes: Primary sources directly authored by Zoroaster are limited to the Gathas. The historical figure of Zoroaster is largely reconstructed through these texts and later traditions. Secondary sources are crucial for scholarly analysis.
